chunks: From him, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abān, from one whom he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Concerning a man who dies as an apostate from Islam while he has children and wealth.
So he said: “His wealth belongs to his Muslim children.”

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: the religion from which apostasy occurred
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: those among his children who are Muslim
key_terms.لِوُلْدِهِ: assigned to his children as heirs
key_terms.مَالُهُ: the wealth belonging to the deceased person
key_terms.مُرْتَدًّا: one who has apostatized from Islam

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the wealth of a person who dies as an apostate in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the estate of a man who dies having apostasized from Islam. It states that his wealth is to go to his children who are Muslim, indicating the relevance of religious status in inheritance rulings.
